# gof

**Model diagnostics based on cumulative residuals.**

`gof` checks fitted models by accumulating residuals along a covariate or
the fitted predictions. It compares the observed curve with simulated null
curves and reports Sup and L2 test p-values, helping identify patterns that
a coefficient table may miss.

Methods cover `lm`, Gaussian/binomial/Poisson `glm`, Gaussian structural
equation models fitted with `lava`, and `lava` ordinal regression. Additional
procedures provide joint inference across orderings, SEM residual-distribution
checks and binomial/Poisson parametric bootstrap calibration. Each method's
help page states its assumptions and support limits.

This is a maintenance fork of Klaus K. Holst's
[original gof project](https://github.com/kkholst/gof). The fork's changes
have not been released on CRAN or merged upstream. Original authorship,
license and method citations are retained.

The 1.4.0 development version adds diagnostics for `ordinal::clmm` mixed
models with a single grouping factor or nested random effects. `lava`
remains required; `ordinal` is optional. The
[mixed-model guide](https://github.com/Marimuda/gof/blob/feature/clmm-integration/vignettes/ordinal-mixed-models.Rmd)
explains parameter polishing, cluster multipliers and calibration limits.

## Installation

Install release 1.3.0, including its worked guides, from GitHub:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Marimuda/gof", ref = "v1.3.0",
                        dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The package requires **R >= 4.1 and C++17**. Source installation needs R's
development toolchain, including the matching Rtools on Windows or command-line
developer tools on macOS. Building guides from a checkout also requires Pandoc
supported by `rmarkdown` (at least 2.8). Supplied source archives contain
the built guides.

For reproducible work, retain the release tag or exact commit and record it
with your analysis results.

To try the 1.4.0 development branch, including ordinal mixed-model diagnostics:

```{r development-installation, eval=FALSE}
remotes::install_github("Marimuda/gof", ref = "feature/clmm-integration",
                        dependencies = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The mixed-model path is experimental and **not release-qualified**. Its completed
slow cohort failed the prespecified size/refusal criteria. The larger confirmation
study is still running; the mixed-model guide retains the adverse results.

## Example

This example fits a straight line to a curved relationship. The seed makes
the data and Monte Carlo calculation reproducible.

```{r example}
library(gof)

set.seed(42)
d <- data.frame(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 200))
d$y <- 1 + 0.5 * d$x + 0.7 * d$x^2 + rnorm(nrow(d))

diagnostic <- lm(y ~ x, data = d) |>
  cumres(variable = "x", R = 499, plots = 25)

as.data.frame(diagnostic)[c("variable", "test", "statistic", "p.value")]
```

```{r diagnostic-plot, fig.alt="Observed cumulative residual curve compared with 25 simulated null curves along x; the curved mean omitted from the fitted model produces a systematic residual pattern."}
diagnostic |> plot(idx = "x", legend = "type2")
```

A small p-value indicates that this aspect of the fitted model deserves
attention. A large p-value does not establish that the model is correct.
Sup and L2 summarize the same residual process in different ways. A reported
zero means no simulated statistic reached the observed value; it is not an
exact probability of zero. Increase `R` for greater Monte Carlo precision.

`as.data.frame()`, `summary()` and optional `broom::tidy()` methods expose
results and diagnostic metadata. Native `|>` pipelines and base-R tables
do not require tidyverse packages.

## Statistical scope

The multiplier procedures use asymptotic approximations. Rare events, severe
imbalance or limited information can produce poor calibration even with many
rows. Fitted-value ordering also depends on numerical fitting accuracy;
unresolved comparisons withhold inferential p-values while retaining curves
for inspection. Genuine ties enter together. Prespecified fixed covariate
orderings avoid the estimated-coordinate ambiguity.

`cumres_joint()` shares multipliers across selected orderings to provide
family tests and simultaneous null reference envelopes. Separate marginal
`cumres()` simulations cannot be combined into joint draws.
`cumres_normality()` is an asymptotic Gaussian SEM procedure; its supported
fits require complete, independent-subject data. It does not establish that
every latent or measurement error is normal.

`cumres_bootstrap()` supports fixed design orderings for canonical binomial
and Poisson models. Fitted-null calibration remains approximate. Simulation
under genuinely specified means permits a distinct Monte Carlo test. Failed
and unresolved refits remain in the accounting. See the guides for weighted
and grouped responses, ordinal aggregation, boundary fits and availability
rules before interpreting results.

The fixed-order bootstrap study retained 637,000 records across 106 cells.
All 14 eligible primary cells met the project-specific 4–6% practical
criterion; two greenflies cells met only an upper-bound criterion. Stress
cases retain failed fits, conservatism and an observed 6.62% L2 rejection
rate in one leverage scenario. These results support the declared design
and parameter points, rather than exact 5% control or universal validity.
The assessment was model-assisted, without independent human review or expert
endorsement. The [validation guide](https://github.com/Marimuda/gof/blob/release/1.3.0/vignettes/finite-panel-validation.Rmd)
reports the full scope, provenance and limitations; compact evidence is
installed with the package.
